rule: You count as a consumer if you bought the goods or service for your own use. Buying for resale or for a commercial purpose is excluded.
evidence: for resale or for any commercial purpose

rule: A defect is any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard of goods.
A deficiency is any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of performance of a service.
A complaint must be filed within 2 years from when the cause of action arose. A late complaint is accepted only if the commission is satisfied there was sufficient cause for the delay.
evidence: within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen

rule: You can file at the District Commission where the seller works or has a branch, where the cause of action arose, or where you live or work.
evidence: complainant resides or personally works for gain

rule: A complaint can be filed electronically.
The commission should ordinarily decide whether to admit a complaint within 21 days of filing.
The commission tries to decide a complaint within 3 months of the seller receiving notice, or 5 months if goods need lab testing.
evidence: within a period of three months

rule: If the complaint succeeds, the commission can order the seller to remove the defect, replace the goods, return the price, pay compensation, and in some cases pay punitive damages.
evidence: return to the complainant the price

rule: The District Commission hears complaints where the value paid is up to Rs 50 lakh.
The State Commission hears complaints where the value paid is above Rs 50 lakh and up to Rs 2 crore.
The National Commission hears complaints where the value paid is above Rs 2 crore.
There is no filing fee for complaints where the value paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.
ref: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020, r.7

rule: A seller on an online marketplace cannot refuse to take back goods or refuse a refund if the goods are defective, deficient or spurious, not as advertised, or delivered late.
A seller on an online marketplace must have a grievance officer who acknowledges a complaint within 48 hours and resolves it within one month.
An online store selling its own stock cannot refuse to take back goods or refuse a refund if the goods are defective, deficient or spurious, not as advertised, or delivered late.
Online platforms must pay accepted refunds within the timeline set by the Reserve Bank of India or another competent authority.
Send the seller a written notice asking for the refund, with a deadline (usually 15 days). The Act does not require this, but it creates a record and often settles the matter.
ref: Common practice, not a legal requirement

rule: Register a grievance with the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or use consumerhelpline.gov.in. It tries to resolve the issue with the company before any case.
ref: National Consumer Helpline, Department of Consumer Affairs

rule: If it is still unresolved, file a complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in with your bill, order details, and messages with the seller.
ref: e-Jagriti portal (online filing is allowed under s.35)
